Subject: Re: Spike in p99 / retries impacting checkout - urgent

Elena/Team — quick triage notes from the traces we pulled during the call: 

Findings (short):
- Impact is scoped to ~12% of CardinalPays requests that include long history payloads (median context length ~3.1k tokens for impacted requests). p95 sits in expected range but p99 shows heavy tail due to some workers holding onto large KV caches and experiencing cache churn.
- Worker pool logs show elevated queue lengths on pool-id w-23 and several transient OOM-resistant GC pauses on a small subset of machines.
- Theres evidence of request fan-in on a subset of routing keys leading to backpressure; autoscaling did not immediately compensate because the workload is bursty and long-lived.

Suggested immediate mitigations (we can apply now if you approve):
1) Temporarily reduce max_concurrency for CardinalPay routing key from 16 -> 8 for 24 hours to reduce inter-request queueing.
2) Bump prefix-cache TTL and pre-warm dominant prefixes we observed in your traces (will improve KV hit rate).
3) Route heavy-history requests to a warmed dedicated sub-pool (w-45) for the next 48 hours while we stabilize.

Risk/notes: (1) reducing concurrency will increase per-request latency for short requests in the very short term but should reduce p99 and retries overall; (2) routing change may increase cost slightly for the dedicated pool.

If youre comfortable we can schedule the changes immediately and monitor closely. Ill also open INF-4721 follow-ups to track longer-term remediation.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
